originality.rationale: The all-length all-temporal-period bijection is a genuine statement-wise extension beyond the published individually enumerated Rule 18 two-cycles, Rule 126 four-cycles and Rule 18 first odd eleven-cycles. Stricker 2023 reports an identical maximal cycle-length envelope for a four-rule class, not an exact recurrent conjugacy or per-orbit basin transfer. Wolfram 1983 reports transformations giving similar long-time densities, not the displayed labelled periodic-point bijection. The standard \(AB/BA\) algebra is not asserted novel; the explicit two-rule factorization and its rotation/basin consequences are the research claim.
residual_risks: Wolfram (1983) reports straightforward transformations of rules 18,122,126,146 at the level of asymptotic densities; a different earlier source may explicitly state the full Rule 18/126 periodic-core equivalence.
Martínez et al. (2010) publisher PDF was unavailable; only accessible author manuscript sections and abstract were inspected. An uninspected passage could conceivably contain a related identity.

General AB/BA isospectrality for finite maps is classical and is not itself new; novelty is conditional on the specific domain-wall/OR factorization and complete spatiotemporal and basin consequences not already having been published.
An independent external mathematical and priority audit has not been performed.

value.rationale: Rules 18 and 126 are canonical distinct nonlinear elementary cellular automata, studied in parallel in the primary literature. Rather than another small-case count, the theorem identifies an exact isomorphism of their entire recurrent permutations at every spatial size and preserves the full spatiotemporal symmetry inventory. The per-orbit parity-basin law shows why their full-state statistics can differ, with a complete \(n=4\) witness, and transfers every future exact primitive-orbit classification between these rules. This is a structural relation with motivated invariants, not a routine numerical increment or a relabeling symmetry.
